newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST-Italy July PPI seen falling to 0.4% yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Italy July PPI seen falling to 0.4% yr/yr.

text.p: Italian producer prices should continue to fall in July even though to a lesser degree than in previous months, a Reuter poll of 10 analysts said on Wednesday.
But they said the falling trend, reflecting a stronger lira and relatively subdued commodity prices, could soon be over.
Analysts saw producer prices rising by 0.4 percent from a 0.6 percent increase in June and a 9.2 percent rise in July 1995. In May 1996, PPI had risen 1.3 percent year-on-year.
On a monthly basis, analysts see PPI falling 0.04/0.05 percent after a 0.2 percent fall in July (and in May 1996) and a 0.2 rise in July 1995.

"The decline should, once again, be driven by intermediate goods, while manufactured goods prices are likely to continue to show a positive month on month figure," Bank of America said in a research note. Analysts also noted that stagnating demand for investments is also putting a brake on PPI.

In July, the effects from petrol price hikes have not yet filtered through and the producer price index will start feeling the impact of this in August. Also, in the longer term, labour costs could start having an effect on PPI, analysts said.

"The increase in labour costs will be attributable to two factors: the renewal of metalworkers' contracts, which will mean higher wages, and a fall in productivity because of the economic cycle," Paolo Casadio, analyst at Credito Italiano, said.
National statistics body Istat will publish July producer price as well as July WPI data on Thursday, September 19.
